title: SIMT execution: threads, warps, blocks, grids and SMs
description: How a GPU maps a grid of blocks of threads onto streaming multiprocessors that run threads in lock-step groups of 32 (warps), and what warp divergence costs.

title: GPU memory hierarchy
description: Registers, shared memory, L2 cache and HBM: the orders of magnitude of size, latency and bandwidth, and why data movement rather than arithmetic is usually the bottleneck.

title: Memory coalescing and shared-memory bank conflicts
description: Why a warp's loads should touch consecutive addresses, how to count global-memory transactions, and how shared-memory banks serialise conflicting accesses.

title: Occupancy
description: How registers, shared memory and block size limit the number of resident warps per SM, and why high occupancy helps hide latency but is not a goal in itself.

title: Tiling and the tiled matrix multiplication kernel
description: Staging tiles in shared memory so that each global-memory element is reused T times; the memory-traffic model of naive versus tiled matmul.

title: FLOPs, bytes and arithmetic intensity
description: Counting the arithmetic and the memory traffic of an operation and dividing one by the other.

title: The roofline model
description: Attainable performance as the minimum of the compute roof and bandwidth times intensity; the ridge point; classifying matmul, softmax, layer norm and attention as compute- or memory-bound.

title: IO-aware attention (FlashAttention)
description: Why standard attention is memory-bound, and how tiling with an online softmax removes the N-by-N round trips to HBM without changing the result.

title: Amdahl's law for pipelines
description: The overall speed-up when only a fraction of the time is accelerated, and why the unaccelerated part (data loading, launches, host code) sets the ceiling.

title: Reading a profiler timeline
description: GPU idle gaps, kernel launch overhead, host-to-device copies and data-loader stalls: how to diagnose where a training step spends its time.

title: Number formats for deep learning: fp32, tf32, fp16, bf16, fp8
description: Sign, exponent and mantissa bits of each format, their range and precision, and which one suits which part of training.

title: Loss scaling and master weights
description: Why fp16 gradients underflow, how a (dynamic) loss scale fixes it, and why optimisers keep fp32 master weights.

title: Training-memory accounting
description: Bytes per parameter for weights, gradients and Adam state under fp32 and mixed precision, plus the activation term that scales with batch, sequence length and depth.

title: Gradient-checkpointing trade-off model
description: Memory (n/k)*a_in + k*a_layer versus a 4/3 compute factor, and the square-root spacing that balances them.

title: Gradient accumulation
description: Reaching a large effective batch with several small micro-batches by summing scaled gradients before one optimiser step.

title: Kernel fusion and torch.compile
description: Why chains of element-wise operations waste memory bandwidth, and how fusing them into one kernel (what torch.compile does) cuts the traffic.
